criteria.title: Stripe Checkout Session and Payment Attempts
criteria.description: Requirements PAY-01 to PAY-03 work: POST /donations/{id}/checkout is restricted to the donation owner only and for a donation in Pending status, creates a Checkout Session in payment mode, and returns a valid checkout URL. The session carries client_reference_id = donation.Id and metadata containing donationId and campaignId, a single line item with the campaign title and its amount in minor units (long, e.g., 25.00 → 2500) computed on the server from donation.Amount rather than client input, and the currency and success/cancel URLs from StripeOptions. Each session is stored as a PaymentAttempt with status Created and the required fields; a new attempt can be started for a Pending donation, and a non-Pending donation returns 409 Donation.InvalidState. GET /donations/{id}/payment-status returns the donation status and its latest attempt for the owner and Admin, while another user's donation returns 404. Stripe.net code is isolated in Infrastructure behind an abstraction in Application, and the Controller is thin.

criteria.title: Stripe Configuration, Test Mode, and Secret Protection
criteria.description: Requirement PAY-10: The StripeOptions class (secret key, webhook secret, currency, success and cancel URLs) is registered with BindConfiguration, ValidateDataAnnotations, and ValidateOnStart, and the application fails at startup if any setting is missing. Only test mode keys (sk_test_) are used. The secret key and webhook secret (whsec_) come from dotnet user-secrets or environment variables, and appsettings*.json contains placeholders only. No Stripe key or webhook secret exists in the repository or in Git history, and secrets are never logged.

criteria.title: Webhook and Cryptographic Signature Verification
criteria.description: Requirement PAY-04: POST /api/v1/payments/webhook exists, allows anonymous access ([AllowAnonymous]), and is excluded from rate limiting (SRS §6.4). The endpoint reads the raw request body (without [FromBody] or JSON re-serialization) and the Stripe-Signature header, and verifies it using EventUtility.ConstructEvent and the webhook secret from configuration. An unsigned, tampered, or wrongly signed request returns 400 with ProblemDetails and error code Payment.InvalidSignature before any database modification.

criteria.title: Payment Event Handling and Success Flow
criteria.description: Requirements PAY-05, PAY-07, and PAY-08: The checkout.session.completed event completes the donation via the SRS §5.5 success flow in one transaction (donation Succeeded with CompletedAt and ReceiptNumber in format DN-{year}-{6 digits}, attempt Succeeded, amount added to RaisedAmount, and campaign Completed when the goal is reached), and a late payment for an expired or completed campaign is accepted with a warning log. checkout.session.expired sets the attempt to Expired, and payment_intent.payment_failed sets it to Failed with FailureCode and marks the donation Failed when no other open attempt remains. Unknown sessions and unhandled events are logged and answered with 200. The amount in minor units and the currency are compared against the donation, and a mismatch is logged as an error and does not complete the donation. A donation becomes Succeeded only via the webhook and never via the success URL. No PDF generation or email sending occurs inside the webhook request; jobs are enqueued to Hangfire only after the commit.

criteria.title: Webhook Event Deduplication
criteria.description: Requirement PAY-06: Every processed event is stored in ProcessedStripeEvent (EventId as primary key, Type, ProcessedAt) in the same transaction (the same SaveChanges) alongside the event's changes. Sending the same payload twice returns 200 both times, does not increment RaisedAmount a second time, and does not create a second receipt. The primary key on EventId prevents double-crediting even if the same event arrives in two concurrent requests.

criteria.title: API Request Idempotency
criteria.description: Requirement DON-10 and SRS §6.5: POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/donations and POST /donations/{id}/checkout require the Idempotency-Key header, and a missing key returns 400. Each key is stored in IdempotencyRecord (Key, UserId, RequestHash, ResponseStatusCode, ResponseBody, CreatedAt, ExpiresAt). Same key, same user, and same body returns the stored response (same status and same body) without creating a new donation or session, and the same key with a different body returns 422 Idempotency.KeyReusedWithDifferentRequest. Keys expire after 24 hours. Two simultaneous requests with the same key do not create two donations (e.g., a unique index on Key + UserId with the record inserted before executing the action). Errors return ProblemDetails containing code and traceId.

criteria.title: Integration Testing
criteria.description: The DonationHub.Api.IntegrationTests project exists and uses WebApplicationFactory<Program> against a real SQL Server test database (Docker Compose or LocalDB, with Testcontainers as a BONUS), and never uses EF Core InMemory. Tests never call real Stripe or real SMTP: payloads are built locally and signed with a test webhook secret, and the email sender is replaced with a fake. All six scenarios in SRS §6.13 are covered: register and login, create a campaign and donation, webhook success (donation Succeeded and RaisedAmount updated), duplicate event (credited once and 200), invalid signature (400 and no changes), and Idempotency key replay (same response and no second donation). Running dotnet test succeeds without manual steps other than running SQL Server.

criteria.title: README, Submission, and Stub Removal
criteria.description: The temporary endpoint POST /admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded (DON-06) and its handler are removed (PAY-09) with no trace remaining in the codebase. The README is updated for this sprint and includes a How to test Stripe locally section explaining stripe login, stripe listen --forward-to, storing whsec_ via user-secrets, the three stripe trigger commands (checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.expired, and payment_intent.payment_failed), and testing payment with the test card. The sprint-5 tag exists and points to the final commit, and any fixes use a sprint-5-fix tag without moving the original tag.

criteria.title: Explaining Decisions and Trade-offs
criteria.description: The student's ability during review to explain the reasoning behind their decisions and the trade-offs between them and their alternatives, such as: why the webhook is the single source of truth rather than the success URL, what the HMAC signature and timestamp protect, why the raw body must be read, why ProcessedStripeEvent is saved in the same transaction and what happens if the same event arrives twice at the exact same moment, how the unique index prevents two donations with the same Idempotency-Key, why 422 is returned when reusing a key with a different body, why 200 is returned on an amount mismatch, why a late payment is accepted, why jobs are enqueued after the commit, and why integration tests run against real SQL Server rather than InMemory. Answers are graded on genuine understanding rather than memorization.
